scenes.title: A Woman Made of Lamps
scenes.location: The bulk, above a garden in Daly City (Arenya, dreaming). Sunday night, 2:40 a.m.
scenes.summary: In a shared dream in the bulk above her parents' Daly City garden, Arenya watches her aunt Susmithaa, the host of the Sowri line's light spirit, take the form of a woman made of lamps as a faceless four-man collection team draws a magnetic net that snuffs her flames. Abernathy fights at Susmithaa's side as her squire; his lantern strike fails and his light gutters, but he shields the single flame Arenya reaches for and holds. In that moment his voice slips briefly out of cockney into something old: "keep it lit, child." Arenya tries to pin the man in the light grey jacket from her investigation wall and fails. She keeps only the words "left pocket", and his net's filament "counts" her, leaving a cold coin-sized spot on the inside of her right wrist. Susmithaa pours all her remaining light into Arenya's flame. The collection catches only ash, and her last words are a charge: something old is waking, the doors will open, keep it lit, go with all the light you can carry, and look after Abernathy ("He'll say he's looking after you. He's lying"). Abernathy is torn loose and bound to Arenya, and Susmithaa's body collapses by the curry-leaf tree. Arenya wakes at 3:19 a.m. with a warm, clenched fist; Abernathy is filling her kettle and warns her in private to hide the hand and leave the wrist mark alone. At 3:20 Amma calls: Susmithaa is dead at Seton, her window lamp went out with oil still in it, and a polite American in a suit reached the hospital before the family and asked whether Susmithaa had a niece.

scenes.title: Woke
scenes.location: A grey sedan on a quiet residential street in Daly City, 2:52 a.m., half a block from the Sowri house
scenes.summary: Caleb Strand wakes for real in Team Four's grey sedan at 2:52 a.m., half a block from the Sowri house. His Crown implant is burnt but live, and the containment canister at his feet reads "full" but holds only ash. He keeps his face flat and reports the collection to the handler Shepherd (Deception 18). He passes off his still-extended filament as a "residual tether" and folds it back along the line instead of cutting it. That leaves Arenya's wrist tag masked, faint and findable only by him, and the cost is the first bite of Vesper withdrawal. At the on-ramp light on the way to Drop Two, he unbuckles and bails with the canister (Acrobatics 18). The Crown-flat team doesn't pursue; they drive off to report. Over the Crown, Shepherd calls him "Caleb" for the first time in fourteen months, offers to fix him and make him forget, and warns that the folded tether "will unfold." Caleb names Susmithaa, refuses ("I'd rather be scared"), and deliberately heads away from the south-east pull toward the woman so he won't lead the program to her. He hides in a steel storm culvert in a drainage cut, where the Crown goes silent. Withdrawal and fourteen months of memory crash in. He recites his victims aloud (the Tartine man, Yuri, Susmithaa), admits he never learned his teammates' names, and vows to keep the canister of Susmithaa's ash until someone "not them" tells him what it is. The two Vesper doses stay untouched in his left pocket.

scenes.title: Dawn Watch
scenes.location: Cross-cut: the East Peak fire road on Mount Tamalpais at 3:01 a.m., and Ava's apartment in the Inner Sunset at 5:48 a.m.
scenes.summary: At 3 a.m. on East Peak, Kino sensed a warmth to the south, beneath the fog, smelling of burnt butter and church. Ix respects it. Kino failed to track it (Survival 6). Nana told him over the phone that he was "shown it" and should bring "the thing you're not saying" to her table at first light. Kino vowed to the Sleeping Lady, "I'll go where you're looking. You don't have to turn around for me." On the way down, the wind fell into step beside him and his cold birthmark briefly eased, a small sign that she has not abandoned him. At 5:48 a.m. in the Inner Sunset, Ava saw a lit flame in her hands in the reflection in her oven glass while her real hands were empty, and her clocks were frozen at 2:41. She tested it scientifically and found it consistent across angles. It gutters when she holds her breath. Behind her reflection she glimpsed another window: a brass lamp, browning marigolds, and an old woman's hand with a ring on the smallest finger that reached to pinch the wick and stopped (Susmithaa's shrine, unnamed to her). She told it, "Don't go out, I've got you." The vision ended with the clocks resetting to 5:52, and an unseen candle-sized warmth now lives in her palms. Her video shows only a deniable smear of light, and a blank phantom calendar reminder for 3:20 a.m. appeared, the minute Amma called Arenya.

scenes.title: Nana's Table
scenes.location: Nana's kitchen, Daly City: stucco house on the hill above Mission St
scenes.summary: At first light Kino confesses to Nana Itzel that he has dreamed the Sleeping Lady rolling away from him since September and hid it. She already knew. The overturned second cup belonged to Susmithaa Sowri, her friend of eleven years (Thursday tea, too much sugar). Nana felt her die at about 2:45 a.m. and turned the cup over. The "butter and church" smell Kino tracked was ghee and camphor: Susmithaa's passing. Nana reframes the dream: the Lady isn't turning from Kino, she's turned toward a "door," and the light went through it to Susmithaa's unbelieving niece. Kino works through his jealousy aloud ("even if it should've been me") and decides a champion stands beside the door, not in front of it. Nana answers that his gift is night-eyes, which is what a lamp needs, and plans to bring pozole to the Sowri house at two with Kino carrying the pot, in a black shirt, saying nothing. She tells him what "wrong" looks like: someone nobody remembers inviting (made forgettable), the memorial lamp's flame leaning toward someone with no draft, and anyone watching the niece "like they're working out how heavy she is." Ix will stay out in the fog past the porch light.

scenes.title: Seton
scenes.location: Seton Medical Center, Daly City — the family room off the ER, before dawn
scenes.summary: At Seton before dawn, Arenya comforts her mother, who brought Susmithaa's cracked brass lamp and refused to give it up. She hides the cold coin-mark on her wrist with a "steering wheel" excuse while Abernathy warns her that the man at the nurses' station has no light at all, "like a hole in a fence." Malachi introduces himself as "Shawani, Department of Energy," apologizes, and waits in the corridor while Arenya takes ten minutes with her family. Amma recalls Susmithaa's last dinner: her Thursday friend Itzel in Daly City will come with pozole if she dies. Appa (Ravi) reveals that in March Susmithaa warned him to deny any niece to an American who came asking. In the corridor, Malachi and Arenya trade: she shows him the wrist mark (he's never seen one and warns her off doctors and photographs); he says Adonis Quinn was Monolith's founder's cousin, that his "people" are three analysts and a phone, that a polite American asked for Susmithaa by full name at about 3:40 a.m., before the paperwork, and that Susmithaa did not die like the nine freeze victims. Arenya gives him her burner number; he'll call once tomorrow. She takes custody of Susmithaa's phone (it buzzed repeatedly at 3 a.m. and once at dawn). The lamp stays warm to her touch, and her right fist begins to loosen for the first time.

scenes.title: Pozole
scenes.location: The Sowri family home, Daly City, 2 p.m. the same day
scenes.summary: At 2 p.m. Nana Itzel and Kino bring pozole to the Sowri house. Arenya and Kino meet for the first time. The memorial lamp's flame leans toward Kino as he passes, then trembles between him and Arenya; Nana's verdict is "not only you." A forgettable Lattice watcher who calls himself "Mr. Bell" (grey cardigan, wearing a frost Crown-fragment) appraises Arenya's warm right hand. He notes that Susmithaa's copy of *Curtain* is upside down and leaves a sealed sympathy card. Ix tracks him to a beige rental Camry (plate 7K…R), where he takes off the Crown, bleeds from the nose and makes a reluctant phone report. Abernathy sees a frost-thread tracking tag on the card, so Nana wraps it in her pot towel and hides it in the freezer ("cold hides in cold"). Inside *Curtain*, Arenya finds a March temple receipt for a prayer in her name, with Susmithaa's note: "Ari — The lamp knows who. Itzel knows the rest. Don't let them count you. Keep your hands still until you can't. Then don't." When Arenya holds it, the lamp flame splits in two for one second. Nana explains *los que cuentan* ("the ones who count") and that Susmithaa's light ran down the maternal line and chose Arenya in March. Arenya confesses the truth to Amma, and Kino shows his cold birthmark and accepts the shared door. Amma keeps everyone the night. The scene ends as Susmithaa's phone shows 14 missed calls from Unknown and a new voicemail at 6:12 p.m.

scenes.title: Fourteen Missed Calls
scenes.location: Sowri family home, Daly City: front room by the memorial lamp, evening
scenes.summary: Arenya unlocked Susmithaa's phone with Appa's birthday and played the 6:12 p.m. voicemail on speaker. The caller was "Daniel Hale, Meridian Mutual Life, beneficiary services." He pronounced "Sowri" exactly as the family does, knew the time of death to the minute (3:19 a.m., which the hospital never gave), and asked to "verify the beneficiary in person" (claim ref MM-031944). Kino saw the lamp flame duck small and blue on the word "her," and his birthmark pulsed. Amma says Susmithaa never mentioned insurance; Appa is evasive. Nana recalled Susmithaa saying in March, "I bought a door, and I put Ari's name on it." Kino failed to spot what Ix was watching, but heard a car pull away dark. Then the Sowri landline rang. Hale left a second message addressed to Arenya: the policy is real, paid in cash at a Colma office on March 19; meet tomorrow at noon at Serramonte Library, second floor by the periodicals, or he'll "come to you." He signed off with "Keep that hand warm," which links him to Mr. Bell. Under his voice, a second voice was counting "eleven, twelve," stopping on "hand." Kino heard it, and Arenya unconsciously wrote it in her margin. Frost formed on the freezer seal where the phone and tracking card are hidden. Nana explained that they count the ones who carry, and saying the number aloud means they've moved from hunting to collecting: "Twelve is you." Everyone sleeps at the Sowri house under the lamp. Ix went alone to scout Serramonte. Arenya has decided nobody goes to the meeting yet; she wants to check the Colma office.

scenes.title: What Ix Brought Back
scenes.location: Sowri house, front room, Daly City (small hours)
scenes.summary: Ravi gave Arenya the three papers Susmithaa left: the Meridian Mutual "welcome" letter numbering her 11 and Arenya 12, her notarized torn NO, and a farewell note. The note said "Writing is not keeping," don't sign, verify or give your full name in a room they chose, and asked Arenya to feed Kino, apologize to Amma about the will, and make Itzel tell the frightening parts. Nana Itzel revealed el Contador, a fair, never-erring clerk-spirit born of the 1912 removal of SF's dead to Colma and the stone-yard shed ledgers. Grey "beneficiary" men read its books and collect. In March she witnessed Susmithaa's salt-and-candle no under the shed door. It was entered, and it bought seven months: "a no buys time, not freedom." A second mark in the salt, two strokes side by side, means dos testigos: a contested entry stays open until two stand for it. Arenya told Kino that if it comes to that she'd want it to be him, and he accepted, though not tonight. Hale's calls are understood as pressure to make her name herself. The landline is unplugged, nobody goes to Serramonte at noon, and the plan is breakfast, then Colma in daylight, with Kino walking the stone yard first and Arenya at the gate. In the bond, Abernathy honestly found his memory of "Mark it so it can be found again" walled off clean, "like somebody tidied up after me." The sun mark in Arenya's palm sank back. The family slept together under the lamp while Nana kept watch.

scenes.title: The Stone Yard
scenes.location: A monument-carving yard off Mission Road, Colma, mid-morning
scenes.summary: At the Esposo Monument Co. yard in Colma, Kino walked first with permission ("Con permiso, vengo a ver, no a tomar") while Arenya stayed at the gate with Nana. The yard is a ruled ledger page. Twelve rows of granite blanks run to the shed, which stands as the heading, and a margin file of blanks lines the left fence. Row 11's margin holds Susmithaa's old salted chisel stroke (her contested March no). Row 12's margin stone is polished and holds a single pencil stroke, a witness of one, waiting for a second. At the shed wall Kino heard el Contador, the same dry counting voice from Hale's voicemail, reading back "Doce. Testigo: una. Falta una." It then silently asked him "¿Y tú?" Kino wanted badly to say yes. He refused to answer by word or gesture, turned his gaze to Arenya to mean "not mine to give," and backed away. The clerk followed his look to Arenya and made a tick: referred. A pencil dot now sits beside the rule under the 12 in Arenya's palm, marked "come back to this." Abernathy confirmed the hot-brass smell returned for half a second at the gate, and the clerk ruled him a blank "not yet" line. Leaving, they saw Mr. Bell's empty beige Camry (7K…) parked across Mission Road with a validation slip from Colma Notary & Mail, likely the "Colma office" of the March 19 policy. Tito Boy remarked on "a lot of visitors" this week.
